questions.q: What is a PABX?
questions.n: PABX is the standard term for a private telephone network used within a company or organization.

questions.q: What is the common telephone cable used in the Philippines?
questions.n: RJ11 is the standard modular connector and cable used for single-line telephone connections.

questions.q: Which brand is a known provider for security systems?
questions.n: Visonic is a globally recognized brand specializing in wireless security and intrusion protection systems.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a floor raise (raised floor) system?
o: To provide additional structural reinforcement to the building
To elevate the room to prevent flooding from outside
To easily use floor boxes without cutting the floor slab
To act as a primary reservoir for fire suppression water
questions.n: A raised floor creates a plenum space for electrical and data cabling, allowing for flexible outlet placement.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear depth of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: According to BP 344, 1.40 meters is the minimum depth required to accommodate a wheelchair user comfortably.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: The minimum internal width of the elevator car must be 1.10 meters according to BP 344.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the grab bars or railings inside the elevator?
o: To hang maintenance equipment during cleaning
To prevent people from leaning on the elevator mirrors
To provide support and stability for persons with disabilities (PWDs)
To serve as a decorative trim and aesthetic accent
questions.n: Handrails are essential for providing balance and stability to users during the movement of the elevator.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of the door of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: The door must provide a clear opening of at least 800mm (0.80m) to allow for wheelchair entry.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the beam in a slab-beam relationship?
o: To increase the weight of the floor for acoustic insulation
To support the slab and transfer the loads to the columns
To hold the pipes and conduits in place
To act as a decorative element between the ceiling and floor
questions.n: Beams act as the primary structural members that receive gravity loads from the floor slabs.

questions.q: What will happen if the beam is removed in a slab-beam relationship?
o: The ceiling height will simply increase with no structural impact
The slab will fail or sag due to lack of structural support
The columns will automatically take the load directly
The slab will become stronger due to less weight from the beam
questions.n: Removing the beam breaks the load path, likely causing the slab to exceed its flexural capacity.

questions.q: What connects a beam to a column in steel construction?
questions.n: Clip angles or seated connections using channels are standard methods for joining steel beams to columns.

questions.q: It is the waterstop that expands when in contact with water.
questions.n: Bentonite is a clay-based material that swells significantly when hydrated, creating a watertight seal in joints.

questions.q: What do you call the type of proofing that resists water pressure (hydrostatic pressure)?
questions.n: Waterproofing is designed to withstand hydrostatic pressure, unlike damp-proofing which only resists moisture.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent cap?
o: To stop the smell of the sewer from reaching the roof
To prevent birds, debris, or rain from entering the vent pipe while allowing gases to escape
To increase the water pressure within the drainage system
To connect the vent pipe to the water supply line
questions.n: A vent cap protects the terminus of the vent stack from blockages and external elements.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent stack in the sanitary drainage system?
o: To filter the water before it enters the public sewer
To provide a backup path for water when the main drain is clogged
To provide air circulation and prevent siphonage of trap seals
To serve as the main pipe for carrying solid waste to the septic tank
questions.n: Vents balance the pressure in the pipes to ensure water seals in traps remain intact.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a cleanout?
o: To provide a location for reading the water meter
To allow for the injection of soap into the sewer lines
To provide access for clearing blockages in the drainage pipes
To serve as an overflow point when the septic tank is full
questions.n: Cleanouts are capped openings that allow plumbers to insert snakes or rods to clear clogs.

questions.q: What is the required slope in percentage for a 100mm sewage pipe?
questions.n: The standard minimum slope for pipes 100mm and smaller is 2% (approx. 20mm per meter).

questions.q: What is the most effective type of door to use for acoustics?
questions.n: Mass is critical for sound attenuation; a solid core provides much better blockage than a hollow one.

questions.q: What acoustic treatment is used on concrete to prevent the transmission of vibration?
questions.n: Isolators break the mechanical path of vibrations between the equipment/surface and the structure.

questions.q: What wall construction is best for acoustic rooms (e.g., recording studios)?
o: Double wall with air gap and insulation
Plywood on both sides of a single stud
questions.n: This 'mass-air-mass' system effectively de-couples the two sides, significantly reducing sound transmission.

questions.q: What is the best room size/proportion for acoustics to avoid standing waves?
o: A cube with equal height, width, and length
Longer length (avoiding equal length and width)
questions.n: Non-parallel surfaces and varied dimensions prevent sound waves from reinforcing each other (standing waves).

questions.q: What is the characteristic of granite?
questions.n: Granite is formed from the slow crystallization of magma below Earth's surface, making it intrusive igneous.

questions.q: What is the most commonly used sedimentary rock in construction?
questions.n: Limestone is widely used as a building stone and is a primary ingredient in the manufacture of cement.

questions.q: According to the building code, what is the maximum height of a retaining wall before requiring a formal design?
questions.n: Retaining walls exceeding 1.50m in height generally require structural analysis and a building permit.

questions.q: According to the building code, what is the required overturning factor of safety for a gravity wall?
questions.n: Structural codes typically require a factor of safety of 1.5 against overturning for retaining walls.

questions.q: Which among the choices is used for cementitious waterproofing?
questions.n: Thoroseal is a well-known brand of heavy-duty, cement-based waterproofing coating.

questions.q: What roofing is best to used for standing seam?
questions.n: Standing seam profiles use concealed fasteners and allow for thermal expansion, making them high-performance.

questions.q: What roofing material requires more maintenance over time?
questions.n: Wood is organic and susceptible to rot, fire, and pests, requiring frequent treatment and replacement.

questions.q: What helps with the tensile strength of a roof?
o: Structural steel members like Girder, HSS, or C-Channel
questions.n: Steel is excellent in tension and provides the necessary strength to resist uplift and wind loads.

questions.q: How many live wires are used for a three phase electrical system?
questions.n: A three-phase system utilizes three separate alternating currents, each carried by a 'hot' or 'live' wire.

questions.q: What color is commonly used for the live wire in a single phase electrical setup?
questions.n: In modern standards, Brown (IEC) or Black (older/US) are common colors for the 'hot' wire.

questions.q: For a three-way switch circuit, how many switches are commonly used?
questions.n: A 3-way setup allows control from 2 different locations (e.g., top and bottom of stairs).

questions.q: What is the purpose of concrete cover?
o: To act as a waterproof membrane for the concrete
To protect reinforcing steel from corrosion and fire
To increase the compressive strength of the rebar
To provide a smooth surface for painting the slab
questions.n: The concrete surrounding the rebar provides alkalinity to prevent rust and acts as thermal insulation during fire.

questions.q: What helps with the ductility of concrete?
o: Increasing the amount of water in the mix
Using a higher ratio of sand to gravel
questions.n: Ductility is the ability to deform without breaking; steel reinforcement provides this to otherwise brittle concrete.

questions.q: What is the ratio of Class AA concrete?
questions.n: Class AA is a rich mix used for underwater or high-strength applications, defined by this specific ratio.

questions.q: What helps with creating a seamless connection for frameless glass?
questions.n: Clear silicone sealants are used to bond glass edges while maintaining visual transparency.

questions.q: What connects glass to structural steel?
questions.n: U-channels are often welded or bolted to steel to receive and secure the glass pane.

questions.q: What glass door is commonly used for retail shops?
questions.n: Frameless doors provide maximum visibility into the shop, which is ideal for retail display.

questions.q: Used in narrow hallways and stairwells where access is limited, what is the best window to use when its only purpose is to let light pass through?
questions.n: Fixed windows do not open, making them ideal for spaces where ventilation isn't needed or operable hardware would be obstructed.

questions.q: What is used to create a seal between pipes to prevent leaks?
questions.n: Gaskets are mechanical seals that fill the space between two or more mating surfaces.

questions.q: What connects two different sizes of pipes?
questions.n: A reducer is a fitting used to transition from a larger pipe diameter to a smaller one.

questions.q: What is the device used to cover the hole in the wall for pipes?
questions.n: An escutcheon is a decorative metal plate or flange used to cover the gap where a pipe enters a wall.

questions.q: What is the purpose of mortar in masonry construction?
o: To add a glossy finish to the wall
To provide insulation against cold weather
Adheres bricks together and distributes load
questions.n: Mortar binds masonry units into a single structural element and provides a cushion to distribute pressure.

questions.q: Which anti-stain and acid-resistant material is best used for kitchen countertops?
questions.n: Sintered stone is extremely dense and non-porous, making it highly resistant to stains, acids, and heat.

questions.q: Which part of a fire detection system detects and alerts fire from fire detectors?
questions.n: The FACP is the 'brain' that receives signals from detectors and triggers the alarm notification devices.

questions.q: What is the typical angle of repose for dry materials like sand?
questions.n: The angle of repose is the steepest angle at which a sloping surface of loose material is stable.

questions.q: What is the minimum bar diameter used for a tied column?
questions.n: Structural codes typically mandate at least 12mm diameter for the main vertical longitudinal bars.

questions.q: What type of test is used for measuring soil moisture?
questions.n: The oven-dry method is the most accurate way to determine water content by comparing wet and dry mass.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness of a concrete footing?
questions.n: Standard codes typically require a minimum thickness of 250mm to ensure proper depth for rebar and strength.

questions.q: What is the minimum depth of a footing below ground?
questions.n: Footings must be placed at a depth sufficient to reach stable soil and avoid surface disturbances, often starting at 600mm.
